Samir — thanks for the conversation this morning. Vantage is asking for a 24-month reserved capacity commitment but is pushing for protection on GPU pricing volatility; their legal team proposed a market-indexed break clause and an upfront discount that would partially be refunded if market prices move below a defined threshold.

Attached: a one-page request from Vantage (Vantage_HLTH_term_request.pdf) and their sizing numbers (vantage_capacity_numbers.xlsx). Key asks summarized: 
- 24-month reserved pool (A100-equivalent) with monthly invoicing
- A 12% standard discount off list, with a conditional rebate if the GPU market index falls >15% versus start-of-term
- A put/call style break clause at the 12- and 18-month marks tied to index moves

We need to align on: guardrails we can offer without exposing Redwood to open-ended downside, whether finance is comfortable holding an "escrowed" discount, and any fleet provisioning changes if we accept a higher burst profile.

Can Marcus/karthik/dylan weigh in on (a) how to size the dedicated pool for this profile, (b) what discount/escrow structure we can tolerate, and (c) approvals required (finance + legal + revenue ops)?

Next steps I propose: short internal call today to align and then a 30-minute call with Vantage tomorrow.

Thanks,

Naomi — quick thoughts after a skim of the attachments: I like the idea of an escrow-style mechanism but we should limit rollback exposure and operational complexity. High-level proposal: 

- Escrow discount mechanics: Redwood invoices at the contracted discounted rate; a portion (up to 40% of the discount amount) is held in escrow and reconciled quarterly against a mutually agreed GPU spot index. If index drops >15% cumulative, we refund from escrow up to the escrowed balance; if index rises, escrow is released to Redwood.
- Thresholds & caps: refund cap = 25% of annual committed spend; escrow cap = 40% of discount value; trigger lookback period = 90 days average.
- Sizing impact: with their Q4 spike profile, we should reserve ~35 A100-equivalent steady capacity with a 1.5x burst pool for 6 weeks around product launches. That's a mix of dedicated and autoscale burst.

Risks / asks: finance needs a clear reconciliation cadence and legal will need language around index source and dispute window. Dylan — can you run revenue ops impact (quota, commissions) for the escrow/refund flows? Marissa — heads up in case this needs an exec approval for an exception to our standard discount SKU table.

-Marcus
VP, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

Attachment recommended: fleet_sizing_recommendation.xlsx (note: I'm attaching a rough sketch in the follow-up)

Folks — adding the operational/cost scenarios we ran quickly this morning. TL;DR: an escrow works if we bind it to a narrow cap and pair it with a floor/collar to avoid small market noise creating churn. Proposed alternative that reduces risk:

Option A (Escrow + Cap):
- 24-month term, 12% list discount, 40% of discount escrowed, quarterly reconciliation, refund cap = 25% annual committed spend.

Option B (Floor/Collar pass-through):
- 18–24 month term configurable, 10% list discount guaranteed, GPU price floor at start-of-term; if index falls >20% we give an additional 3% rebate (one-time), if index rises >20% we retain full price. Max refund exposure = 12% of annual spend.

Fleet sizing (initial): reserve 40 A100-equivalent steady; enable autoscale burst up to additional 20 units for 8 weeks (marketing launch window). This assumes typical concurrency and a 50% KV-cache hit rate; if Vantage expects colder caches (real-time inference), increase steady pool by +10.

Attached: fleet_sizing_recommendation.xlsx (worked example) and a short cost sensitivity table. If legal wants the index to be a publicly verifiable source, use the "OpenGPU Index" (we can reference in the contract).

Please advise which option we take to present to Vantage. If we pick Option B we materially reduce Redwood downside and should be able to keep standard approval cadence; Option A will require a finance sign-off for the escrow account.

-Karthik
Director, Product Economics
Redwood Inference

Attachments: fleet_sizing_recommendation.xlsx (Excel)
